messages:
Harper: FYI customer AcmeApp is seeing 502/504s hitting hosted inference around 03:04 UTC right after an auth token rotation. Repro steps below + logs.

Harper: Repro (from their side):
1) open streaming generation with large payload (~2.5MB)
2) trigger service-side token rotation
3) subsequent requests intermittently get 502 or 504 within 10-30s

Harper: Their curl they used:
```
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <rotated-token>' \
  -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @large_payload.json
```

Harper: Edge logs snippet (from their trace id 01H8XK2...):
```
[envoy] upstream reset before response complete
[nginx] client aborted while waiting for upstream
```

ops-bot: Alert acknowledged: incident-5982. Trace id 01H8XK2 forwarded to eng-sre.

Liam: Can you paste the full edge logs and the upstream (auth proxy) logs? I'm guessing h2 keepalive pool exhaustion + authcache TTL race. Also need connection pool stats (envoy counters) around that time.

Harper: Pasted link to NR dashboard: https://nr.example/trace/01H8XK2
Harper: Upstream auth proxy shows `401` for a subset of connections at rotation time then immediate retries, a few `RST_STREAM`

Olivia: Likely scenario — when auth tokens rotate we still reuse existing HTTP/2 connections that have old Authorization headers in upstream requests, causing auth proxy to reject and upstream to reset streams. With large chunked streaming the client keeps connection open and pool re-use causes collisions. Two quick mitigations: 1) drain connections to upstream on token rotation; 2) shorten connection reuse lifetime for auth-proxied tenants.

Maya: For immediate mitigation we increased keepalive timeout and set per-tenant drain on auth rotate in staging. Can we try bumping `h2_keepalive_timeout` from 20s -> 40s for affected edge pool and enable `auth-header-hash` based connection partitioning?

Liam: Also we should check if envoy/nginx strips or rewrites the Authorization header. If not partitioning, will reuse same conn for different tokens. Suggest change: add small connector-level fingerprint so auth header changes force new upstream conn.

Harper: Customer willing to test. Provided quick repro command they can run after our config change.
Harper: Repro to run (they will):
```
python3 scripts/stream_gen.py --payload large_payload.json --url https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --token <old> &
sleep 5 && rotate-token && curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <new>' --data-binary @small.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Olivia: I'll open a runtime PR to add `auth-conn-partition` flag and a short-term rollback plan. Liam, can you collect envoy stats and increase `max_pending_streams` and tune `conn_pool_size` for that pool?

Liam: On it. ETA 45m for stats + hotfix rollout to staging.

Harper: Customer reported after temp increase to keepalive + enabling drain we saw errors drop >90%. They will run extended test.

Olivia: Adding follow-up item: postmortem if this recurs; long-term fix = partition by auth header and ensure token rotation triggers graceful upstream drain.

Harper: Thanks team :thumbsup:
